knowledge:
- key_parameters: maxDist=Maximum genomic distance between motif pairs to consider as candidates in prepareCisPairs() (default is 10^6 bp) ;; formula=Formula specifying the predictive variables for the logistic regression model in predLoops() ;; betas=Coefficients of the logistic regression model in predLoops() (uses a default model optimized for several TF ChIP-seq datasets if not specified) ;; cutoff=Minimal prediction score threshold to report loops in predLoops() (set to NULL to report all candidates without filtering) ;; colname=Modifies the column name for experimental support in addInteractionSupport()
- alternatives: Experimental methods like Hi-C or ChIA-PET are mentioned as the gold standard for measuring chromatin conformation, but they are elaborate, expensive, and have limited resolution/availability compared to ChIP-seq.
- when_to_use: Use this package when high-resolution chromatin looping data (like Hi-C or ChIA-PET) is unavailable for a specific cell type or condition, but ChIP-seq data (e.g., CTCF or other transcription factors) and motif locations are available.
- pitfalls: Reading bigWig files using addCovToGR() or addCor() is not supported on Windows systems; Windows users must manually provide ChIP-seq signals around motif sites as a NumericList object (e.g., motifs$chip <- l). Evaluating prediction performance on the same dataset used for training (without cross-validation) is insufficient and can lead to overoptimistic results.

workflows.name: predict_loops_default_model
workflows.intent: Predict chromatin looping interactions from CTCF motifs and a ChIP-seq bigWig file using the default pre-trained model.
input: motifs.hg19.CTCF.chr22 (GRanges object containing CTCF motif locations with -log10 transformed p-values in the 'score' column)
workflows.stages: 1. Load CTCF motifs ;; 2. Read ChIP-seq coverage at motif sites using addCovToGR() ;; 3. Build candidate motif pairs within a distance threshold using prepareCisPairs() ;; 4. Compute ChIP-seq signal correlation between pairs using addCovCor() ;; 5. Predict loops using predLoops() ;; 6. Export predicted loops to a BEDPE file using export.bedpe()
workflows.code:
library(sevenC)

# load provided CTCF motifs
motifs <- motif.hg19.CTCF.chr22

# use example ChIP-seq bigWig file
bigWigFile <- system.file("extdata", "GM12878_Stat1.chr22_1-30000000.bigWig", 
  package = "sevenC")

# read ChIP-seq coverage 
motifs <- addCovToGR(motifs, bigWigFile)

gi <- prepareCisPairs(motifs, maxDist = 10^6)

# add ChIP-seq coverage and compute correaltion at motif pairs
gi <- addCovCor(gi)

loops <- predLoops(gi)

library(GenomicInteractions)

# export to output file
export.bedpe(loops, "loop_interactions.bedpe", score = "pred")

workflows.name: train_custom_prediction_model
workflows.intent: Train a custom logistic regression model using known experimental loops and use it to predict chromatin loops.
input: motifs.hg19.CTCF.chr22 (GRanges object containing CTCF motif locations)
GM12878_HiCCUPS.chr22_1-30000000.loop.txt (Text file containing known experimental loops in Rao et al. format)
workflows.stages: 1. Load CTCF motifs and read ChIP-seq coverage using addCovToGR() ;; 2. Build candidate motif pairs using prepareCisPairs() and compute ChIP-seq signal correlation using addCovCor() ;; 3. Parse known experimental loops using parseLoopsRao() ;; 4. Annotate candidate pairs with experimental interaction support using addInteractionSupport() ;; 5. Fit a logistic regression model using glm() ;; 6. Predict loops using the custom model coefficients and formula in predLoops()
workflows.code:
# load provided CTCF motifs
motifs <- motif.hg19.CTCF.chr22

# use example ChIP-seq coverage file
bigWigFile <- system.file("extdata", "GM12878_Stat1.chr22_1-30000000.bigWig", 
  package = "sevenC")

# add ChIP-seq coverage
motifs <- addCovToGR(motifs, bigWigFile)
  
gi <- prepareCisPairs(motifs, maxDist = 10^6)

# add correaltion of ChIP-signal
gi <- addCovCor(gi)

# parse known loops
knownLoopFile <- system.file("extdata", 
  "GM12878_HiCCUPS.chr22_1-30000000.loop.txt", package = "sevenC")

knownLoops <- parseLoopsRao(knownLoopFile)

# add known loops
gi <- addInteractionSupport(gi, knownLoops)

fit <- glm(
  formula = loop ~ cor_chip + dist + strandOrientation, 
  data = mcols(gi), 
  family = binomial()
  )

# add predict loops
gi <- predLoops(
  gi,
  formula = loop ~ cor_chip + dist + strandOrientation,
  betas = coef(fit),
  cutoff = NULL
)
